clue.text: A very strong atmosphere of romance

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud or strong
an atmosphere or ambience is an air

explanation.surface: A romantic setting with a powerfully charged mood, like a candlelit dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a romance, a relationship outside the everyday.

clue.text: Use the wrong sort of tackle, perhaps

definitions.text: Use the wrong sort of tackle, perhaps

parts.words: Use the wrong sort of tackle, perhaps
parts.note: reads like choosing the wrong fishing gear, but means an illegal challenge in football

explanation.surface: An angler grumbles about picking unsuitable fishing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' suggests fishing kit; in football an illegal tackle is penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Committing an illegal tackle in a sports match is to commit an infringement, a verb sense.

clue.text: Formerly together

definitions.meaning: in the past, once upon a period
simultaneously, all at the same moment

explanation.surface: Two words that seem to describe a couple who used to be partners.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'once, in the past' and 'simultaneously', two distinct idiomatic senses.

clue.text: One who picks the winning ticket goes up for the prize

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word drawer is read from bottom to top

parts.words: One who picks the winning ticket
parts.note: the person who draws a raffle ticket is a drawer

explanation.surface: At a raffle, the person drawing the lucky ticket heads up to collect the prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize is a recompense or award, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Famous symphony, also part variation

indicators.note: a musical variation reworks a theme, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous symphony is said to include a section of variations.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ALSO PART gives the name of Beethoven's Sixth Symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Symphony No 6 is known as the Pastoral, a celebrated named work.

clue.text: It goes on all the time

definitions.text: It goes on all the time

parts.words: It goes on all the time
parts.note: sounds like a complaint about something tediously constant, but describes a machine that never stops

explanation.definitionFit: A hypothetical machine running forever without energy input is the classic impossible device of physics.

clue.text: Fish cooked as diners required

indicators.note: cooking alters food, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fish prepared exactly as the restaurant's customers asked for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small oily fish of the herring family, often sold tinned, are a kind of fish.

clue.text: Scotch governor?

parts.note: looks like a Scottish ruler, but is the bar device that regulates measures of Scotch whisky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' suggests a Scottish official; in a British pub a whisky bottle is fitted upside down with a gadget dispensing a fixed measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's measuring dispenser controls how much spirit is poured, so it governs the whisky.

clue.text: An eye-opener for many every day

definitions.text: An eye-opener for many every day

parts.words: An eye-opener for many every day
parts.note: an eye-opener is usually a revelation, but here something that literally wakes people each morning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-opener' means a surprise; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedside device that rings to wake sleepers literally makes them open their eyes each morning.

clue.text: Tight contest in which the winners manage to pull back

definitions.text: Tight contest in which the winners manage to pull back

parts.words: Tight contest in which the winners manage to pull back
parts.note: sounds like a comeback in a close match, but the winning team literally pulls a rope backwards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull back' suggests recovering a deficit; here the rope is taut and hauled backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In this rope-pulling team contest the rope is tight and the victors drag it back towards them.

clue.text: Ceremonial trial rearranged about the middle of January

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the central letter
the letters of trial are put in a new order
the central letter of the seven-letter word January is picked

explanation.surface: A trial is rescheduled for mid-January with full ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' turns TRIAL into RITAL, and 'about' puts it around U, the middle of January.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a set ceremony; used as an adjective, ritual means ceremonial.

clue.text: Returns from work

parts.note: reads as coming home after the job, but means money gained through employment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like a verb about going home; it is a noun for yields.
explanation.definitionFit: Money gained from wages or salary, as opposed to investment yield, is the tax term for pay from a job.

clue.text: Dilapidated hamper has butter over it

indicators.note: in a down entry, the butter's letters sit above the hamper's

parts.note: something that butts with its head, like a male sheep, a ram
to hamper is to restrict, to shackle

explanation.surface: A battered picnic hamper has had some butter spread on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' and 'butter' look like picnic nouns; a butter here is a creature that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramshackle means rickety and falling apart, a synonym of dilapidated.

clue.text: They were wise, putting the scholar before the soldier

indicators.note: putting one piece before the other sets the order of the two

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a scholarly degree holder
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Sensible people put academics ahead of the military.
explanation.definitionFit: The Three Wise Men of the Nativity story are known by this collective name.

clue.text: Exploit at length for a beneficial purpose

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it
in full detail, fully

explanation.surface: Making the most of something thoroughly for a good cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to helpful or productive effect is acting to a good end.

clue.text: It's intended to make one's pile last longer

definitions.text: It's intended to make one's pile last longer

parts.words: It's intended to make one's pile last longer
parts.note: sounds like saving a fortune, but means padding that protects a carpet's pile

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' suggests a heap of money; a carpet's pile is its tufted surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt laid beneath a carpet cushions it and reduces wear on its tufts.

clue.text: Spoils Worcestershire opener's time at the crease

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first

parts.note: in cricket, a batsman's spell at the crease is an innings

explanation.surface: A Worcestershire opening batsman's long stay at the crease ruins things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a verb but is a noun for gains. Worcestershire is an English county cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoils are gains or loot, money taken from a contest or bet.

clue.text: Particular pieces muddled by a learner

indicators.note: these letters are confused and put in a new order

parts.note: L, from the L-plate shown by a learner driver

explanation.surface: A learner driver has jumbled up some particular pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is a formal synonym for special or particular, as in 'of especial note'.

clue.text: Try to avoid the lowest possible score

definitions.meaning: to dodge or evade something, verb sense
in cricket, a score of nought by a batsman

explanation.surface: Every batsman hopes to escape getting out for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is a verb sense; a cricketer out for nought has scored the zero of that name.

clue.text: It's found in a rediscovered deed and revised

indicators.note: one piece is discovered inside the other
the letters of deed are rearranged as if recovered in a new form

explanation.surface: Something turns up in a newly rediscovered deed that has been amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' reads as 'it is', but only the word it is used; 'rediscovered' makes EDED, which 'found in' wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: An edited text has been revised, corrected and amended for publication.

clue.text: It shows the priorities for strikers

definitions.text: It shows the priorities for strikers

parts.words: It shows the priorities for strikers
parts.note: suggests a union's list of demands, but strikers here are cricket batsmen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' suggests industrial action; in cricket the batsman facing the bowler is the striker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket team's batting list shows who goes in first, second and so on.

clue.text: Modern city can split round ancient one

indicators.note: the tin is split open and wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: a can is a tin
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's usual old city

explanation.surface: A modern metropolis encircling the ruins of an older one.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a present-day industrial city in northern Italy, Piedmont's capital.

clue.text: Social workers write article on good man arising

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the saint's letters read upwards

parts.note: ST, saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: Social workers write an article about a good man coming to prominence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' reads as care staff; it describes insects that live in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects live in organised colonies with worker castes, so they are social workers.

clue.text: Potential risk one in France may take in winter

definitions.text: Potential risk one in France may take in winter

indicators.note: potential means latent in another form, so these letters can be rearranged

parts.note: un is French for one

explanation.surface: A winter outing carries potential danger for a person in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' turns RISK into SKIR. As a whole the clue describes a slope taken in winter, risky for one in the French Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: A downhill piste is something a person may risk descending in the snow season.

clue.text: Mean to arrest man, eventually

indicators.note: arresting someone holds them, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
he, a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A determination to detain a man, finally achieved.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finally or ultimately, after everything, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Poet writes new sonnet about New York

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other piece
the letters are made new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A poet composes a fresh sonnet about New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like a description of the poem but is the anagram signal, giving TENSON; 'about' wraps that round the state's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Dislike of French cricket

parts.note: de is French for of
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Seems to name a disdain for French-style cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a long international cricket fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe or hate, a stronger synonym for dislike as a verb.
